$comment: SR-136 license policy encoding, verbatim from docs/plan/04-security-program.md §6.13. Consumed by tools/ci/security_gate.py license evaluation. Do not restate SR-136 prose elsewhere (C-16.5) — this file *is* the machine-readable copy.

needs_approval.$comment: LGPL requires security + owner approval per SR-136. A licence in this list fails the build with CI-SEC-003 unless an accepted-risk entry (security/accepted-risks.yaml) names the exact finding id and is unexpired.

prohibited.$comment: Prohibited in shipped code per SR-136. Dev-only tooling may use GPL where it is not distributed — see dev_only_exceptions below.

dev_only_exceptions.$comment: Packages that carry a prohibited licence but are dev-only tooling, never distributed with shipped code (SR-136 dev-only carve-out). The gate matches each entry as the exact string '<name>@<version>' (npm), so a version bump needs a new entry. Reasons: caniuse-lite (CC-BY-4.0) is browser-support data read by browserslist at build time, never distributed; truncate-utf8-bytes (WTFPL) is a dev-only transitive of the desktop packaging toolchain, never distributed; @napi-rs/lzma-linux-x64-gnu@1.5.1 is MIT per the npm registry (license: MIT) and the upstream repo github.com/Brooooooklyn/lzma, reported Unknown because rollup's platform binary is not installed on the scanning host (expires at the GA cut, 2027-03-25: remove or re-justify by then; a canary test, test_repo_register_dev_only_exception_expiry_canary, fails the build after that date, because the schema has no per-entry expiry or reason field). The gate cannot check that a package is dev-only: that is established by `pnpm why -r` at review time, and only the production licence collection (checked with these exceptions disabled) restores a check. The match key is not ecosystem-qualified, so an entry would also exempt a PyPI distribution of the same name@version. Tracked by #5628.
